## ps2/DETAIL_PRESETS
# Optional detail presets — October 17 continuation


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/DETAIL_PRESETS.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `d975750da76c55fc7f71684d29e5ea2a106060d3b6b5b7845a2f3ebfe09b4e75`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


## Player success and scope

Original must preserve the game's image, memory changes and native settings.
High should delay car simplification; Maximum should retain the highest permitted
loaded car model throughout the supported visible race range, including split
screen. Maximum's optional 2P projection/fog range restoration must show complete
geometry without new holes and retain playable native 1x speed; 4x is a separate
performance gate. This does not promise new assets, infinite terrain, persistent
debris, or unchanged performance on every track/hardware.

## Situation and recovered evidence

shows far=575 with configured draw distance1150 and native selected car indexes
1..4. Function00211318 indexes `{1,1,2,2}` using view-count minus1, so the car
LOD multiplier is the same for1P and2P, not doubled in2P. Camera builder00212B58
divides configured distance by view-count and derives both projection and fog
from that quotient. These are distinct causes of detail/range reduction.

Native minimum index is1 for the observed cars. Index0 is not their highest
complete playable car; force-LOD0 would lose geometry/parts. The existing loader
hook already validates table ownership, levels, minimum, model handles and
ordered finite thresholds, respecting clone sharing and native register effects.

## Implementation and research

Reuse the existing `EOD_CAR_LOD_MULTIPLIER` mechanism, also published as
[bf6a575](https://github.com/catsandsoup/eod-recomp/commit/bf6a575) on the optional
`upstream/car-lod-multiplier` branch. A numeric environment override takes
precedence over the whole Detail preset, including range, allowing exact Original
comparison via value1. No change is posted to the upstream repository.

`[Video] Detail=original|high|maximum` defaults to Original and requires restart.
High multiplies positive car thresholds by3. Maximum scales the first native
permitted threshold to at least1,000,000 scaled distance units (>800x the largest
native far plane1150), preserving ordered finite distances and native minimum,
count, handle arrays, flags, wheel/damage logic and shadow tables. Invalid tables
remain unchanged. This retains the highest permitted model for normal finite
visible race distances; it does not bypass culling or force a numeric model0.

Maximum also scopes a2x configured-distance input only around native camera
builder00212B58 when view-count is exactly2 and the input is finite in(0,1150].
Native projection and fog both receive the original1P range. The source distance
word is then restored exactly, preserving guest registers and unrelated callers.
Cinematic overrides and unsupported view counts remain native. No global view
count is forged, no frustum test is bypassed, and no streaming pool is expanded.

Rechecked RoadTripAdventure-recomp's
[overrides.cpp](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/overrides.cpp): its camera/frustum changes
are scoped to verified consumers. Its runtime ABI and game addresses differ, and
it has no transferable generic EOD car-LOD implementation. Follow the scoped
consumer pattern using the existing EOD hook and native camera/fog calculation.

Debris persistence and extra1P-only visual passes are excluded: the prior trace
found a per-view12.5/count budget and fixed pool initialization around00310000,
not a proven safe lifetime-only switch. A1P-only call at00218D24 also has
unresolved semantics. Changing global view count to unlock these would affect
simulation/resource limits. Persistent debris needs pool ownership/recycling,
collision, lifetime and exhaustion evidence first. Existing debris/physics,
texture promotion and track traversal remain native.

## Validation

Results follow the bounded, headless/muted build and game gates; no physical
hardware/player acceptance is implied by CPU contracts or one scripted scene.

- Release build and signed Mac app succeeded. All 47 CTest cases pass, including
  eight LOD runtime modes, full guest-memory Original identity, native minimum
  boundaries, invalid thresholds and camera range/view-count boundaries.
- Maximum completed the scripted 6600-vblank two-player race at both 1x and 4x,
  headless and muted. Native 640x448 race windows: median59.9, minimum59.3 FPS.
  At4x (2560x1792 internal), last six five-second race windows: median58.55,
  minimum49.3 FPS. Loading/countdown also dips into the low50s. Maximum therefore
  does NOT meet a locked60FPS 4x gate; it remains optional and Original remains
  the default. These are window averages, not instantaneous minimums.
- Native Maximum trace:640 model-selection samples retained native minimum1,
  visible distances through431 units, far plane1150;20 valid car tables loaded.
  Both players take distinct scripted paths. Reviewed captures show complete
  nearby cars/damage and more complete distant cars; no obvious holes or fog
  seams in this bounded scene. Other tracks/physical play remain unverified.
- Replaying the identical baseline GS capture on unmodified8e74d28 and candidate
  produced byte-identical4MiB VRAM and2560x1792 screenshots. Separate live
  Original runs did not produce identical hashes; full live-run byte identity
  is not claimed. CPU contracts prove the disabled hook's memory behavior;
  same-capture replay establishes renderer parity, not game-hook execution.
  replay-results.json,parity-original/final.ppm}. Comparison images in the
  recovered documentation process notes are actual game captures at the same scripted moment,
  with minor separate-run timing variation possible. No5x/6x tests were run:



## ps2/GS_ALPHA_ORDER
# Vulkan alpha-test pass ordering


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/GS_ALPHA_ORDER.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `5cbd14a2ce484f633fb78ffbefae74815159a14ada1e33ca57a793645d5a41a4`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


The GS applies the alpha test and AFAIL action per primitive, in draw order.
The Vulkan backend implements tests that can still write on failure with two
passes. Rendering all passing fragments of an entire batch followed by all
failing fragments reorders primitives. In particular, a font shadow's failed
FB_ONLY fragments can overwrite a foreground glyph drawn later in the batch.

The backend now emits passing and failing draws consecutively for each
triangle, line or point. Sprite quads are already expanded into two triangles;
their nonoverlapping triangle coverage retains the same order. Vertex upload,
target acquisition and binding remain batched. Ordinary one-pass draws retain
their existing batching. Two-pass batches issue more GPU draw calls; gameplay
performance remains a separate integration check.

The asset-free `alpha_overlap` case in `gs_pixel_fixture.cpp` reproduces the
problem with two overlapping rectangles sharing state and Z=1: black with alpha
64 fails GEQUAL 96 and writes FB_ONLY, then cream `(200,200,160)` with alpha 128
passes. Both use depth GEQUAL in a Z16S buffer. The expected interior is cream.
The previous Vulkan batch order produced `(100,100,80)`; software and corrected
Vulkan both produce `(200,200,160)`. `VulkanGSPixels` asserts this result using
actual Vulkan and fails rather than accepting software fallback.

A local, uncommitted retail menu replay independently reproduced hollow font
interiors. Its glyphs use a 256×256 PSMT4 atlas, MODULATE/TCC, source-alpha
blending, alpha GEQUAL 96 with FB_ONLY failure, depth GEQUAL Z16S at Z 115, and
DATE disabled. Corrected Vulkan produces solid glyph interiors. Within the
matched title/instruction text region, 691 bright software-reference pixels
had mean absolute RGB error 19.43 before and 0.90 after; pixels with error over
40 fell from 147 to 0. These measurements establish this alpha-order defect and
its font reproduction, not complete renderer equivalence. UNORM blend rounding
and other GS limitations remain separately documented/tested. No retail data,
replay or screenshots are committed.

Run with an available Vulkan device:

```sh
EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1 ctest --test-dir build-mac -R '^VulkanGSPixels$' --output-on-failure
```

## Exact constant-depth FB_ONLY batching

For FB_ONLY failure with identical vertex Z throughout a batch, depth writes can
be deferred if the depth test is GEQUAL or ALWAYS and DATE is disabled. Color is
written for both alpha-test outcomes. With GEQUAL, an earlier passing fragment
can only change an accepted destination depth from at most Z to Z; every later
fragment at that same Z keeps the same visibility. ALWAYS is independent of
destination depth. The backend therefore draws all color in native primitive
order with depth writes disabled, followed by an alpha-passing depth-only draw.
This preserves both final color and depth. Strict GREATER, varying Z and other
AFAIL actions retain ordered per-primitive passes.

`AlphaPassOrder` compares native-order color/depth against deferred depth over
50,000 deterministic randomized cases, including all eight alpha-test modes,
16/32-bit Z ranges, coverage gaps, overlapping fragments and varying alpha.
Concrete counterexamples show why strict GREATER and varying Z are excluded.
Procedural Vulkan cases independently check these fallback paths.

The local font replay remains byte-identical to the ordered fix while draw
calls return from 2,204 to 52. The five-frame race replay remains byte-identical
at both internal scale 1 and 6, but calls only fall from 183,923 to 183,879: most
race geometry has varying Z and cannot use this fast path. A bounded three-run
6x replay gave warmed best 261.9 ms before and 258.9 ms after; this does not establish
an overall gameplay speed improvement. Further performance work must preserve
the ordered fallback for overlapping primitives.

## Disjoint varying-depth groups

The remaining two-pass primitives may share passes only while their conservative
physical screen coverage occupies disjoint 16×16 pixel tiles. Bounds include the
vertex shader's half-pixel shift and internal scale, expand by one physical
pixel for raster precision/aliased line/point edges, and intersect the viewport
scissor before integer conversion. Shared edges, crossings and tile overlap end
the group. Rejected bounds never mutate the proof. Empty clipped geometry has
no coverage. Every group is contiguous in native primitive order, and overlapping
groups keep PASS/FAIL order. Bound textures remain the same immutable sources
already selected for the original batch; grouping does not introduce feedback.
`EOD_ALPHA_GROUP=0` retains the ordered per-primitive diagnostic path.

`AlphaPassTiles` checks 128,000 randomized bound insertions plus 256 full image
color/alpha/depth differentials with varying Z, strict/GE depth, all four AFAIL
modes, destination-alpha blending, negative/clipped geometry, crossing bounds,
shared edges and line expansion. Actual Vulkan procedural cases also pass.

The local font image and 6x race output are byte-identical with grouping enabled
and disabled in the same binary. The race capture's draw calls fall from 183,879
to 135,695. In a bounded three-repeat 6x comparison, warmed best replay time falls
from 249.2 ms to 227.6 ms for five captured frames. This is a limited replay gain,
not evidence of 100% gameplay speed. Conservative triangle bounds still prevent
many groups, so significant varying-depth overhead remains.

## Whole-batch alpha outcome proof (main, October 16)

The Vulkan backend now applies the existing alpha-range helpers to actual draw
batches. This adapts PCSX2's `CalcAlphaMinMax` / `TryAlphaTest` approach from
[`GSState.cpp`, revision 685637d30b5eaa8e5d7a587673a17577a92dcb88](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2/blob/685637d30b5eaa8e5d7a587673a17577a92dcb88/pcsx2/GS/GSState.cpp#L6417).
Bounds include every decoded texel in every active mip, after palette/TEXA/AEM
expansion, and live with the immutable cached texture. Rendered/unknown sources
retain 0–255. Vertex and texture bounds have a one-byte interpolation/filtering
guard; the TCC/TFX equation produces conservative final-alpha bounds.

If every fragment passes, one ordinary draw replaces the ordered pass/fail
sequence. If every fragment fails, one draw with the original fail color mask,
blend and depth state replaces it. Mixed/uncertain ranges keep the existing
ordered fallback. Geometry, shader color calculations, simulation, resolution
and frame presentation are unchanged. `EOD_ALPHA_RANGE=0` selects the same-binary
baseline; the proof is enabled by default. All-pass alone removed no draws in
the retail capture; the useful reduction came from proven all-fail batches.

`VulkanGSAlphaRange1x` and `VulkanGSAlphaRange6x` compare all 4 MiB of VRAM with
proof disabled/enabled. They assert actual draw reduction for flat/textured
constant outcomes, FB_ONLY/ZB_ONLY/RGB_ONLY failures and strict/varying depth,
and unchanged draw counts for mixed-alpha and conflicting active-mip ranges.
The test was observed failing before integration (8 draws versus expected
reduction), then passing. The CPU range test independently checks all 524,288
TCC/TFX byte pairs and 100,000 randomized bounds against fragment predicates.
The complete Release build and all 39 CTests pass, including GPU-upload modes
at both 1x and 6x. Independent read-only review found no correctness issue.

The fixed five-game-frame retail race capture at native 1x drops from 143,373 to
102,931 draw calls (28.2%). In alternating, isolated, same-binary measurements
(three runs per mode, four replays each, first replay excluded), warm median
falls from 230.4 to 184.3 ms (20.0% less time). Baseline warm samples were
223.0–243.2 ms; candidate 180.1–193.1 ms. Readbacks remain 58 and submits remain
65. The full displayed race and font images and all 4 MiB of final VRAM are
byte-identical off/on at internal scale 1 and 6. This is evidence for those
captures only, not complete GS fidelity or full-speed gameplay.

Ignored evidence: `work/alpha-range/results.json`, `measured-race-*.log`,
`verify-*.log`, raw comparison VRAM/images and `work/alpha-ctest.log`. Retail
assets, captures and binaries are not shipped. The remaining varying-alpha,
overlapping varying-Z draws and synchronous CPU preservation reads still cost
substantial time. Higher resolution, LOD, widescreen and higher FPS remain
deferred until native play meets the player's acceptance criteria.

The candidate's native 1x/4:3 scripted two-player loop reached 6,600 vblanks and
exited 0 in 110.23 seconds, using isolated memory cards and sparse captures,
headless and muted. Race game/drawn samples were 17.3–32.0 FPS (final 20.2), with
GS busy 97–99% and EE waiting 56–75%. The preceding consolidated run was roughly
13–25 FPS (one 11.2 sample during the transition). These full-loop samples are
not an exact matched-scene performance ratio; use the fixed replay above for
that comparison. Full-speed heavy racing remains unmet, and headless scripted
input cannot establish visible control latency or original-reference fidelity.


## ps2/GS_COLD_PACKET_REPLAY
# Bounded clean-start paraLLEl-GS experiment — 2026-10-16


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/GS_COLD_PACKET_REPLAY.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `d381d54bc4a73be2f54e60a628d98e88adb88dde6eb98eb055c2c388de217aee`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


## Player outcome and scoped question

The player still needs accurate native 1x/4:3 rendering at original game speed,
without frame skipping or changes to simulation. This experiment asks whether
Road Trip's existing paraLLEl-GS can consume actual EOD packet traffic before a
live-backend migration is considered. It does not establish race performance,
whole-game parity, latency or player acceptance.

## Capture added to the existing runtime

`EOD_GS_DUMP_COLD_START=N EOD_GS_DUMP=work/boot.gsd` records the initialized
GS state **before the first queued command**, followed by the existing command
stream through vblank N. N must be explicitly supplied in 1..6600. Recording
stops at a complete command boundary if it reaches 256 MiB. It is disabled by
default and does not change the `EODGSD01` ABI or existing renderer behavior.
The ordinary `EOD_GS_DUMP_AT` capture remains available. Automated captures must
be headless and muted; use a bounded `--frames` count as well.

The existing vblank-only capture could not prove empty CLUT/vertex/partial
transfer state. The clean-start probe rejects any State other than `gs_init`'s
zero state with IMR=0xff00 and PRMODECONT=1, plus nonempty paths/active transfer.
It uploads initial VRAM and processes all four existing command kinds using
`GSInterface::gif_transfer`, mutable `PrivRegisterState`, `get_gif_path`, and
`vsync`. No guessed arbitrary retail snapshot import is used. Hacks and
supersampling are disabled; the default GSOptions uses X1.

The scratch probe remains outside the product: its build currently refers to
local oracle/reference checkout paths. No third-party renderer code, binary,
retail packet data or image is committed. Publishing a portable standalone tool
and reviewing its dependency licensing remain separate work.

## Observed CRT bootstrap

A real bounded `--log gs` run observes `SetGsCrt(interlace=1, mode=2, ffmd=0)`.
`runtime/kernel/kernel.cpp` forwards the BIOS syscall parameters unchanged.
`gs_set_crt` records SMODE2 but currently ignores mode, so no SMODE1 reaches the
packet dump. Without a bootstrap, paraLLEl-GS reports unknown video format.

Official [PS2SDK graph_mode.c](https://github.com/ps2dev/ps2sdk/blob/master/ee/graph/src/graph_mode.c)
maps BIOS mode 0x02 to NTSC and its SMODE1 table uses CMOD=2, LC=32.
[GS_SET_SMODE1](https://github.com/ps2dev/ps2sdk/blob/master/common/include/gs_privileged.h)
defines their bit positions. The probe's explicit
`--observed-ntsc-mode2` option reuses exactly the two fields supplied by
[Road Trip's presenter boundary](https://github.com/silentsudin/PS2Recomp/blob/818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4/ps2xRuntime/src/lib/gs/gs_pgs_backend.cpp#L492).
This is a documented mode bootstrap for this observed NTSC run, not a claim to
restore every BIOS CRTC register or support other display modes. The production
runtime's CRT semantics were not changed.

## Actual evidence

Source baseline: `b15d0d9` plus the default-off capture hook. Dependency pins:
Road Trip `0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8`, PS2Recomp
`818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4`, paraLLEl-GS
`60e6cacead2dece90c4d85ebb5ae750d4aace143`, Granite
`16e7395f6a4858c1783dbf6f521f90b9d5f82ac5`. All GPU work was exclusive,
headless and muted on the Apple M2 Pro through the existing MoltenVK oracle.

- A generated pristine-state fixture containing two GIF packets on different
  paths, a path reset, privileged writes and a vblank succeeds. Its complete
  4-MiB VRAM is byte-identical to EOD Vulkan.
- Actual boot through 30 vblanks/79 GIF calls succeeds, with byte-identical
  4-MiB VRAM against EOD Vulkan. The image is still black at that point.
- A movie prefix through 464 vblanks/464,504 GIF calls succeeds and produces
  an inspected Monster Games logo framebuffer. Its complete VRAM matches EOD
  Vulkan. This upload-heavy workload says little about race rendering.
- Numeric scripted Start taps at 40, 100, 200 and 400 skip the opening movie.
  The bounded trace reaches the title/main-menu transition at vblank 618.
  After trimming the 1,616-byte tail after its last complete vblank, all three
  renderers consume the identical 268,203,140-byte file. It contains 49,416 GIF
  calls and six path resets. paraLLEl-GS produces an inspected 640x448 CRTC
  title image with the explicit observed-NTSC bootstrap.

| Identical completed prefix | Time | Comparison limit |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| paraLLEl-GS, second replay | 951.6 ms | Includes vsync/CRTC and final GPU drain; excludes file parsing/final CPU output |
| EOD Vulkan, second replay | 781.4 ms | Existing replay/display path, including requested final VRAM output |
| EOD software, one replay | 3338.9 ms | Existing software path with eight raster workers |

These timings are diagnostic, not a matched race benchmark or a speedup claim.
PGS's completed CRTC image versus EOD's final displayed image has RGB mean
absolute differences of (6.66,6.45,6.08)/255 against software and
(6.89,6.70,6.35)/255 against Vulkan. Complete VRAM differs in 989,808 and
1,275,417 bytes respectively. The raw circuit framebuffer also differs. The
visible title/menu transition and double-buffer/display ownership need tracing;
known blend precision differences alone do not explain or validate these
results. Neither existing EOD backend is a hardware oracle. **Parity is not
established.** Earlier smaller raw-framebuffer differences from the untrimmed
trace must not be substituted for these completed-prefix diagnostics.

Local evidence is under ignored `work/pgs-cold-*`: capture/replay logs, complete
prefix, VRAM, raw framebuffer and CRTC PPMs. Retail artifacts stay local.
The normal Release runtime rebuild and all 41 CTests pass with the hook present.
The installed app remains the validated b15d0d9 production renderer: this later
change adds an opt-in diagnostic capture only, not a player-facing renderer fix.

## Concrete next success

The existing wheel is technically viable for real EOD command streams, but is
not yet a proven full-speed solution. The relevant mechanism remains eliminating
EOD's CPU local-to-local transfer round trips by letting paraLLEl-GS own GIF
rendering and VRAM. Road Trip's `Submit`, `LoadClut` and `UploadImage` callbacks
are empty; `BeginTransfer` pulls GPU VRAM only for local-to-host. EOD currently
calls `hw::vram_needed` then copies local-to-local pixels on the CPU.

Before a live adapter: provide bounded streaming/compressed clean-start capture
and replay to reach a representative short race window without collecting many
GiB of raw boot traffic; explicitly preserve observed CRT metadata; trace the
completed-frame image/VRAM discrepancies; measure the warmed race window with
GPU completion included and identical native scanout requirements. The 256-MiB
capture ceiling was intentionally retained here. A live adapter additionally
needs authoritative VRAM/CPU-read ownership, SIGNAL/FINISH synchronization,
reset handling, presentation, and frame-skip/timing integration. Arbitrary saved
retail state still has CLUT/queued-vertex/partial-image continuation gaps; Road
Trip itself omits CLUT/open-strip restore based on its own game's rewrite
behavior. No such assumption has been made for EOD.


## ps2/GS_CPU_WRITE_PRESERVATION
# GS CPU-write preservation


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/GS_CPU_WRITE_PRESERVATION.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `6bd890197ca5ff79be32c95fc606e8f9e886b386f6a8b421678a10d95adf1476`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


Verified experimental source branch: `macos-cpu-preservation`. It is not merged
into `macos` because of the measured performance regression below.

A CPU upload can replace only part of a page last rendered on the GPU. Dropping
that page's owner without reading its remaining contents back loses untouched
pixels. The original partial-upload fixture differed from software in 8,188 of
4,194,304 VRAM bytes. This is a proven ownership defect; it has not been tied to
the cited.

## Actual supplied bytes, ordered writes

Host upload notifications now occur in `xfer_data`, for pixels actually supplied
by that call. TRXREG declares a future rectangle and cannot justify discarding a
page whose bytes may never arrive. IMAGE qwords contiguous in one GIF call are
coalesced; split/interrupted packets continue normally. Incomplete 24-bit pixels
wait for the remaining source bytes. Each supplied region synchronizes software
raster dependencies and invalidates affected texture memory.

Vulkan flushes earlier queued primitives before CPU reads/writes. It reads back
partial or masked GPU-owned pages before modifying CPU VRAM. Discarding an old
page without preservation requires every storage block to be fully covered by
this actual buffered write, not merely by the declared transfer. CT24/Z24 and
high-byte/nibble formats cannot use that discard proof.

This improves the shared transfer notifications and the Vulkan preservation
path. D3D11 retains its existing partial-page discard/pending-draw behavior and
has not received the Vulkan guarantee.

## Verification — October 16, 2026

- Full Mac build and all 25 CTests pass. `GSPageCoverage` checks 520 randomized
  address cases across 13 formats; `GSTransferChunks` checks 5,000 sequential
  region cases, pending CT24 bytes and interrupted transfers.
- `VulkanGSCPUWrites` and `VulkanGSCPUWrites6x` compare all 4 MiB of VRAM against
  software at 1x and 6x. All 12 asset-free fixtures pass: partial, neighbor,
  pending draw, full page, split chunks, interrupted declared-full upload, CT24,
  high8, high4 low/high, local copy and a partial row spanning two pages.
  Software fallback is a skip, never accepted as Vulkan verification.
- The local corrected font capture is pixel-identical to its reference. The
  five-frame retail race replay is byte-identical to its preceding image.
  This supports those scenes only; screenshots and retail data are not committed.
- Tests/build logs are ignored `work/documentation process-build-cpu-final.log` and
  `work/documentation process-ctest-cpu-final.log`; fixture outputs live in `build-mac/`.

The original flush-only fixture used a point on a separate render target. At
6x the current backend renders one physical pixel, which center-sampled 1x
readback can miss. The fixture now uses a small sprite on that separate target,
keeping the entire-VRAM comparison and transfer semantics intact. Point scaling
is a separate open renderer limitation.

## Measured cost and remaining work

An isolated alternating baseline/candidate test rebuilt the baseline from
`2b60019` and used the same 6x five-frame race dump. Warm baseline replay times
were 211.2–229.5 ms; preservation took 325.0–330.3 ms. Both made 135,695 draw
calls. Preservation added 58 CPU readbacks and increased submits from 7 to 65.
and `timings.json`. This is a correctness fix with a substantial performance
cost, not a speed optimization. It does not meet full-speed 4K multiplayer.

An experimental exact-page coalescing through the existing rectangle helper
still needed 58 readbacks and took 328.5 ms; it was removed. Future optimization
must retain actual-byte ordering and untouched storage, potentially by buffering
writes until a proven complete transfer or preserving CPU/GPU subpage ownership.
Do not drop synchronization based on conservative drawn masks or presumed future
upload bytes. Public fixtures, font output and retail replay must stay correct.

The prior integrated 6x MP run reached vblank 6600 and exited with status 0;
late samples ranged 12.2–29.1 drawn FPS. The preservation build also reached 6600 and exited0, but late samples were
8.1–14.3 drawn FPS, final10.2 drawn /33.4 gameframes /60.2 vblanks persecond.
The main Mac build is restored to the preceding renderer; this candidate remains
available for correctness/performance development without making play slower.

## Published experimental GPU transfer continuation

Branch `macos-gpu-transfers` keeps complete physical 256-byte blocks on the GPU,
using existing GS swizzle mappings and upload rectangles. A paired write-complete
notification ensures uploads happen after CPU data is actually written. Partial,
masked, unsupported or ambiguous ownership retains conservative preservation.
CPU-known-block validity avoids unnecessary readbacks until GPU writes invalidate
that proof. The latest texture lookup checks whether all requested mip storage is
already CPU-current before acquiring a GPU view.

Latest checkpoint: Release build and all 26 CTests pass, including 22 procedural
full-4-MiB software/Vulkan comparisons at 1x and 6x plus the independent 1,904-case
block mapping test. This is experimental source, not merged to `macos`. Earlier
GPU patches moved stalls between CPU writes and texture reads without a material
race speedup. The latest early texture-validity selection has not been measured
on the retail race replay. Do not claim native full-game correctness or faster
racing from these fixtures alone. EOD_GPU_UPLOADS=0 selects the same-binary host
preservation baseline. See the main branch's docs/DEVELOPER_HANDOFF.md for current
owner priorities, build instructions and branch map. No disc/capture data shipped.


## Consolidation into main

All source above is now included in `main`. The default uses the conservative
host preservation path. Complete-block GPU uploads require `EOD_GPU_UPLOADS=1`;
`0` or unset keeps them off. The unified CTest suite explicitly tests both modes
at 1x and 6x. Historical branch names above identify experiments only; developers
do not need to merge or check out those branches. Alpha-range proofs are now integrated; see `docs/GS_ALPHA_ORDER.md` for measured
all-pass/all-fail draw elimination and unchanged preservation read counts.

## Native 1x transfer follow-up after command caching — October 16

**Success first.** The player still needs heavy carnage at original timing and
full speed, native 1x/4:3, with FrameSkip=0. This investigation's narrower gate
was fewer forced CPU/GPU readback dependencies with identical displayed pixels
and all 4 MiB of VRAM, plus an isolated replay/native improvement. Reduced
readback counts alone do not establish that outcome.

**Situation.** At source `b15d0d9`, alpha rejection and Vulkan command caching
are enabled. The complete-block transfer experiment remains off by default.
An isolated same-binary comparison collected nine warm measurements per mode
(three alternating mode rounds, four replays per process, first discarded).
Conservative preservation measured 165.4 ms median; `EOD_GPU_UPLOADS=1`
measured 174.4 ms. Readbacks fell from 58 to 24 and submits from 65 to 31,
but this sample did not become faster. These measurements are separate from
the command-cache comparison and must not be combined into one speedup.

**Task and action.** Trace the remaining 24 reads before designing another
optimization. All were CPU-write preservation for indexed uploads aliasing a
PSMZ16 surface. A group of three 16x16 PSMT4 rectangles and one 8x8 PSMT8
rectangle recurred six times in the fixed five-game-frame capture. A throwaway
planner proved actual supplied physical bits formed
complete owner pixels even when they did not fill a 256-byte block. Its CPU
storage oracle passed the two retail-shaped aliases and rejected partial owner
pixels. The renderer used existing `upload_rect`, retaining all other GPU data.

**Result.** This prototype merely moved the dependency: subsequent 8x8 PSMT4
writes supplied partial owner pixels, and texture consumers could not prove
sub-block CPU equality. It still made 24 reads (18 CPU preservation, six texture
reads), 31 submits and 102,931 game draw calls. Its nine warm samples measured
177.2 ms median. The prototype was removed; no unproven optimization or new
runtime flag shipped. Ignored investigation logs, timings and rejected patch
are under `work/transfer-followup/`. The default remains conservative host
preservation, and the existing complete-block mode remains opt-in.

The existing complete-block on/off modes retained byte-identical race/font
images and complete 4-MiB VRAM at both 1x and 6x in this follow-up. The prior
`b15d0d9` baseline already passed all 41 CTests; the final change here is only
this evidence/handoff documentation. No app replacement was needed.

The existing complete-block opt-in also completed an isolated native 1x/4:3
two-player run: 6,600 vblanks, exit 0, 110.788 seconds, race drawn samples
17.6–35.1 FPS (final 17.9). Late GS worker occupancy was 99%, EE waiting
76–77%. Scene variation prevents a matched native speed claim. These counters
remain framebuffer-flip heuristics/CPU occupancy, not original-cadence proof or
hardware GPU utilization. Native full-speed player acceptance remains unmet.

**Reuse decision and next decisive test.** Rechecked Road Trip's pinned
[paraLLEl packet backend](https://github.com/silentsudin/PS2Recomp/blob/818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4/ps2xRuntime/src/lib/gs/gs_pgs_backend.cpp):
original GIF/register traffic reaches `GSInterface`; CPU primitive, CLUT and
image-upload callbacks are empty, and the CPU read boundary synchronizes GPU
VRAM. This avoids reconstructing masked storage ownership in another custom
GS. Reuse the existing local M2 Pro oracle for a cold-boot packet replay spike,
then verify pixel/VRAM fidelity and native timing before adopting a backend.
The current oracle supports canonical procedural state only and deliberately
rejects retail CLUT, partial GIF, queued vertices and transfer continuation;
feeding an arbitrary mid-race EOD dump to it is not a valid comparison.

PCSX2's pinned [Metal download implementation](https://github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2/blob/685637d/pcsx2/GS/Renderers/Metal/GSTextureMTL.mm)
separates scheduling a copy from waiting at its CPU-consumption boundary.
EOD's preservation path immediately consumes the old bytes before writing new
ones, so splitting its copy/wait functions alone does not remove the dependency.
Local-to-local GPU copies also do not address the 24 observed CPU-upload reads.
A custom masked merge would require exact per-bit ownership and preservation
at each scaled pixel, plus finer CPU-validity proofs; it was not stacked onto
this unsuccessful prototype.


## ps2/HUD_EDGE_ANCHORS
# Native race HUD edge anchors


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/HUD_EDGE_ANCHORS.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `ce1dabd4b1c1452e28dbf648c7627280a83046bf744660e352644ebc7e16e729`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


Source and CPU-contract verification checkpoint, 2026-10-16. Rendered acceptance remains
pending. The existing matched 4:3/16:10 image shows real additional scenery but
also shows left position/lap/damage rows and right speed rows inset into the
old 4:3 area. Camera correctness does not establish HUD edge placement.

## Exact target evidence

Disassembled the supported local SLUS_209.10 (CRC32 75BB93EE) with tools/dis.py,
and checked the synchronous global-g_ee generated call convention.

- `00127050` updates the racing overlay, with actual POS/LAP/DAMAGE and KPH/MPH
  strings. It queues the row content via `0011DEE0` (right queue) and related
  native functions. This is game HUD evidence, not a classification of rendered
  texture coordinates.
- `0011CA48(a0=view)` calls `00119888`, `00119F40`, then `0011ACC0`.
  `00119888` draws the left row queue at `003C4370`; `00119F40` draws the right
  queue at `003C4600`. Each queue contains native row content, dimensions,
  padding, colour, and slide-animation state. The centred queue is separate.
- For nonnegative viewport IDs, `00119888` obtains its X anchor using
  `0011DC50`, the left endpoint at `003C4310 + view*0x18 + 4`.
  `00119F40` obtains its X anchor using `0011DC30`, the right endpoint at
  `003C4310 + view*0x18 + 8`. Their Y origins use separate accessors.
- `0011D2C8(a0=viewCount)` stores that count at `003C41AC` and builds the
  rectangle table: top+0, left+4, right+8, bottom+12, centreX+16, centreY+20.
  At `0011D550`–`0011D670` it derives the native bounds from 640x480 and the
  actual row/column counts, then applies the original overscan values. Solo
  and the game's two-player horizontal divider both have a full 640-unit X
  span; more views use different columns and are intentionally unsupported.
- `00297498` supplies overscan. Original 4:3 returns top/bottom36 and
  left/right48. Native wide/letterbox flags select different left/right values
  (-58/-53). Thus deriving an inset from an assumed fixed safe-area constant
  or permanently rewriting the table would be incorrect. The wrapper retains
  the actual existing value, including initialization timing and asymmetry.
- The real per-player loop `00101C00` derives the viewport with
  `00211398` and installs it using `0034FAF0` before calling
  `0011CA48` at `00101D34` with the current view ID from HUD state+0x20.
  Native HUD matrix `00297A88` is identity with Z=-365; it retains the active
  native projection. No host GS-vertex transform is needed for the relocation.
  The separate full-screen call at `001063DC` passes view=-1 and is retained.

In the existing comparison, the 16:10 inset is approximately 8.3% of the full
viewport width, consistent with a centred HUD X scale of 5/6. This measurement
is independent corroboration of the shift size, not a new precise calibration.
For the supported full-width view, extending an anchor by
`320 * (1/k - 1)` before that native projection gives 64 native units at 16:10
and 106.6667 at 16:9. After projection these account for the added half-width
without changing row sizes. This is an edge translation; it preserves whatever
border overlap or clipping the original 4:3 panel has.

## Scoped implementation

`src/hle_hud.cpp` wraps only the two semantic row-draw functions. It temporarily
subtracts delta from the selected left endpoint during the left draw, or adds
it to the selected right endpoint during the right draw, calls that original
exactly once, then restores the endpoint's exact original bits. All other
layout words and all native EE return-register and draw-list side effects are
retained. The native row animation continues to consume its own shifted edge;
when a row is sliding, its native animation equation controls its displacement.

`eod_presentation_aspect()` provides the same launch-cached race scope as the
camera hook: 16:9/16:10 qualify only inside `00114020`; title/menu/movie/preview
contexts return 4:3. Stretch/4:3 pass through. Only native count1/2 and a valid
nonnegative view ID qualify. Negative/global, unknown counts, invalid view IDs,
and nonfinite anchors pass through. Centred `0011ACC0`, global rectangles,
world UI, generic sprite/text functions and GS packets are untouched.

`EOD_HUD_EDGE_ANCHORS=0` disables the relocation for same-binary comparisons.
No other value disables it. `EOD_HUD_TRACE=1` enables diagnostics: first eight
calls per side, then every120th, at most32 lines per side. Each line includes
side, view/count, aspect, actual anchor, applied shift, current x/base scales
and caller. Diagnostics are bounded and do not infer HUD element identity from
indexes or screen coordinates.

## Reuse decision

Rechecked RoadTripAdventure-recomp main at
`0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8` and its PS2Recomp submodule at
`818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4`:

- [Road Trip's standalone placement tests](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/tests/wide_layout_test.cpp)
- [PS2Recomp's WideLayout implementation](https://github.com/silentsudin/PS2Recomp/blob/818f279be3f9cdecaa9c7b4a3a7cbe8fe44fd6e4/ps2xRuntime/src/lib/gs/gs_wide_layout.cpp)

Its `place` preserves shape with left/centre/right affine placement.
`flush` groups touching rendered primitives and assigns anchors by thirds;
`transformUnit` infers HUD phase from packet path/state and adjusts scissors.
This is a useful geometry reference, but those Road Trip packet/phase
heuristics are not an EOD semantic proof, and EOD already has verified native
left/right row functions. Adapting the semantic EOD anchors is narrower than
importing that renderer-level classifier, and does not risk world/UI overlap.

## Validation and outstanding acceptance

CPU contract target links `tools/tests/hud_edge_test.cpp` with the
production `src/hle_hud.cpp`, include runtime, runtime/include, src, and runs
separately with no argument and with `disabled`. No graphics or game assets
are involved. upstream integration owns CMake, regeneration, full build and GPU
acceptance; config/hle.txt adds only the two wrappers.

Tests inspect the exact temporary guest-memory delta inside stub originals,
all register bytes after return, restoration of original layout bits, native
memory side effects, distinct viewport anchors/asymmetric insets, unchanged
shape widths, and passthrough for 4:3/Stretch/nonrace, unsupported counts and
negative/out-of-range viewport IDs. A passthrough-only implementation was first
shown to fail the native-edge-shift assertion. Stub originals do not establish
real-game layout or final raster pixels.

Focused local validation: Clang C++17 with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` compiled the
production wrapper and CPU contract. Default, `disabled`, and `EOD_HUD_TRACE=1`
runs each passed all160 original-call cases. `git diff --check` passed. No game
launch, full build, source regeneration, or GPU workload was run by this worker.

Required game acceptance: headless/muted matched solo and 2P captures at
4:3/16:9/16:10, baseline switch off versus on in the same binary, checking each
viewport's position/lap/damage rows and speedometer, native padding/shape,
centred flags and messages, paused overlays, menus/movies and the first race
frames. Inspect EOD_HUD_TRACE to confirm nonnegative viewport IDs and actual
native scales/layout. Unknown/global rows are deliberately unchanged and must
be investigated from real traces if they carry visible edge panels.


## ps2/INPUT_CONTINUATION
# Controller/input continuation (October 17, 2026)


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/INPUT_CONTINUATION.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `e592610298880c51f9c03c9be47e0cf78d60785cf52bb6d6aa16f4f4dc776daa`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


## Player success

With automatic assignment a first pad controls P1, a keyboard can join P2, and a
second pad controls P2. Disconnecting a controller never moves another connected
controller or the keyboard to a different player. Reconnecting a known controller
restores its free slot. Held gas/steering survives countdown/menu context changes;
background windows publish neutral input. Inputs received during GS backpressure
must reach the same vblank's EE pad packet. Physical controller, focus restoration,
motor and switch-to-pixel latency acceptance require hands-on testing.

## Situation/task


blocked every held key until release after a context change, and the keyboard's
default P1 reservation made a first pad P2. Existing actuator DMA support was
already merged and did not need to be reimplemented.

## Action and reuse

- Keep the existing mapper and SDL gamepad mapping/rumble paths. Restrict context
  suppression to Enter/Escape (prevents double menu actions); continuous keys and
  unchanged custom bindings remain active. Focus gates both keyboard and pads;
  focus loss stops motors, and background actuator requests cannot restart them.
- Add `KeyboardPort=-1` automatic default. Without a pad keyboard starts on P1;
  after a P1 pad joins, keyboard stays P2 for the session, including disconnects.
  Explicit `0` (off), `1`, `2` settings and `EOD_KEYBOARD_PORT=none|1|2` retain
  their legacy assignment semantics. `EOD_KEYBOARD_PORT=auto` selects automatic.
  An existing saved `KeyboardPort=1` is preserved: change it to -1 in Settings
  and restart to use the new policy. Its prior provenance cannot be inferred.
- Remember per-port serial, else path, else GUID; never evict a connected pad.
  A waiting third pad can occupy a vacant port. Identical pads without unique
  serial/path cannot be distinguished if both are disconnected; GUID fallback
  restores available matching slots in reconnect order, not physical identity.
- Sample SDL input after GS completion and immediately before EE vblank wakeup.
  Windows retains its existing input/GS/IRQ execution order. No renderer queue,
  frame pacing, prediction or simulation changes are introduced.

Reference checked: RoadTripAdventure-recomp at
`0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8`:
[Players.cpp](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/platform/input/Players.cpp)
remembers device-to-player assignments, and
[Input.cpp](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/platform/input/Input.cpp)
publishes neutral pads/stops motors while unfocused. These patterns fit EOD;
its complete input subsystem does not: it targets a different PS2 runtime,
settings/profile system and ImGui frontend. Adapted the patterns within EOD's
existing code rather than replacing its subsystem. SDL's
[serial](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_GetGamepadSerial),
[path](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_GetGamepadPath), and
[keyboard snapshot](https://wiki.libsdl.org/SDL3/SDL_GetKeyboardState) APIs are
used with explicit fallback/OS focus limitations.

## Result and remaining acceptance

Release build and own signed app succeeded. All 44 CTests passed (none
skipped, 20.59 seconds), including 62 keyboard checks, 92 SDL virtual-pad checks,
and real pad RPC/EE DMA pressure/actuator/freshness checks. Tests reproduced
continuous-key blocking, automatic assignment and reconnect failures before the
fix; removing the focus gates and restoring pre-GS sampling fails the new
regressions. Own app packaging initially failed under Documents due to Finder
resource-fork metadata; packaging succeeded in Application Support instead.

Baseline `ec55ff2` and candidate each completed `tools/test_2p_race.sh` at native
1x/4:3, headless and muted, 6,600 vblanks and exit 0. Both contact sheets show
independent moving players in a split-screen race; race logs reach 59.9 drawn
frames/s. Runs used isolated memory card data.

`EOD_INPUT_TIMING=1`, 38 one-second race windows (vblank >= 4300), before/after:

| Counter (microseconds) | Median before/after | p95 before/after | Maximum before/after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One-second maximum pump gap | 17646.5 / 25217 | 28173 / 48306 | 57783 / 53638 |
| One-second maximum pump + DMA | 24 / 24 | 70 / 367 | 113 / 402 |
| One-second maximum GS block | 18.5 / 43 | 18151 / 31925 | 33840 / 42340 |

These are distributions of per-second maxima, not individual input-event ages.
The pump moved across GS, so its phase and gaps changed; counters do **not**
establish an overall latency improvement. The DMA regression proves the narrower
improvement: input arriving during GS blocking reaches this vblank's packet.
Headless scripts generate no native key events and cannot measure physical or
baseline `work/documentation process-input-baseline/` in the main worktree. Timings are from one
sequential run per build, with scene variation, not a performance benchmark.
Shared mapper changes and the config parser are separable; SDL assignment,
focus and sampling integration belong to the non-Windows platform. Existing
pad actuator protocol support is unchanged. Automated tests do not establish
physical Rock Candy HIDAPI behavior, motor operation, OS key restoration after
focus changes, or physical-switch-to-visible-pixel latency. The next decisive
hands-on test is two real controllers plus keyboard in a local race, unplug/
replug each, hold gas through countdown, then focus away/back and check no stuck
controls or rumble. Identical controllers without device identity remain limited.


## ps2/KEYBOARD_CONTEXT
# Keyboard context in SLUS_209.10


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/KEYBOARD_CONTEXT.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `45f219d5aee2a77c8677b6010fb8cba2440a591d269e011f337749c0235c3515`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


The SDL Racing keyboard preset reads actual game state each pad poll. It does
not infer game state from a frame counter, screenshots, car speed or controller
activity. The Original preset retains the configured PS2 key bindings. Gamepad
input and its Original/Modern selection are independent.

| State | Target producer / consumer evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Driving loop active | `0x00114020` writes `1` to `0x00437BB8` at `0x00114058`, repeats the actual race/update loop, and clears it at `0x001141BC` before returning. Its debug message at `0x00114184` is `game_loop: The Race is over`. |
| Modal menu active | `0x0027C508` saves the previous `0x004A1AD4`, writes its window argument there at `0x0027C5DC`, dispatches input to that window and restores the previous pointer at `0x0027C8A0`. Nested menus therefore keep the modal flag active, including menus inside the driving loop. |
| Title | `0x002BEC08` builds `start.lyt` and `press the START button`, stores its scoped stack pointer in `0x003D7BB8` at `0x002BEDFC` and clears it at `0x002BEE34`. Alternate title `0x002BEE70` similarly sets `0x003D7BBC` at `0x002BEEC0` and clears it at `0x002BEF50`. |

Priority is Title, then Driving if the driving loop is active and no modal
window is active, otherwise Menu. EE RAM is checked for null before reading
these fixed target-specific addresses (the standalone controller diagnostic
has no game RAM). `EOD_INPUT_LOG=1` prints context transitions and all four raw
state words even in headless runs with scripted pad input.

The pad-to-UI event chain confirms actual button semantics: `0x00332938`
extracts pad byte 3 bit 6 (Cross) into state offset `0x20` at `0x00332B44`,
and pad byte 2 bit 3 (Start) into offset `0x40` at `0x00332B68`.
`0x003338D0` edge-detects those states and emits UI key `0x0D` for Cross at
`0x00333A54`, and `0x113` for Start at `0x00333A68`.
The title registers hotkeys for both codes at `0x002BEC70`/`0x002BEC90`.
The movie input consumer `0x003673C0` accepts keys `0x1B`, `0x0D` and `0x113`
(`0x003673F4` through `0x00367420`), so Enter as Cross also skips movies.

Racing preset: menus use WASD/arrows to navigate, Enter accepts, Escape goes
back. Title Enter sends Start alone. Driving uses W/Up for Cross (gas),
S/Down/Space for Square (brake), A/D or Left/Right for steering, and Escape
for Start (pause). Enter has no driving action. Other configured keys retain
their PS2 bindings. Reserved Racing keys override conflicting PS2 bindings,
so Enter never sends Cross plus Start and Space never sends Circle in a race.
Opposite directions cancel to center. Held gas/steering and custom bindings remain live across context changes,
including countdown and temporary modals. Enter and Escape alone require release
before acquiring a new context action, preventing a held Pause from backing out
and a title Accept from also accepting the next menu. Focus loss publishes neutral
keyboard/gamepad state and stops rumble; focus return uses SDL's current snapshot. Original bindings remain independent of game context.

`eod_keyboard_test` exercises these cases and layout config round trips.
The target state evidence above is disassembly evidence; actual full-game
context-transition and physical keyboard checks are separate integration
validation, not established by a pure mapper test.

## Input latency diagnostics

Host events must be pumped before publishing this vblank's IOP pad DMA. SDL's
`SDL_GetKeyboardState` returns its last event-pump snapshot. The former order
(Pad DMA, GS/present, event pump) therefore published a stale key state and
could delay the next refresh behind GS work. The SDL kernel now services GS first, then pumps once and publishes pad DMA
immediately before the existing vblank flags/IRQ. Events arriving while GS
blocks are therefore included in this vblank rather than the next. Quit
returns before publishing pad data. `pad_rpc_test` models queued keydown and
release events and reads the actual pad DMA halves: all three freshness/quit
checks fail with the former order and pass with the corrected order.

For a bounded next-launch measurement, set `EOD_INPUT_TIMING=1`. SDL logs native
key event age and the age when the keyboard is sampled (up to 256 lines).
On macOS the bundled SDL Cocoa driver derives these timestamps from NSEvent's
timestamp. The kernel prints per-second maximum pump gap, combined pump/DMA
duration, and time inside `gs_vblank` (up to 120 lines). These diagnostics
measure event delivery/publication and GS blocking; they do not claim to
measure physical-switch-to-visible-pixel latency or game physics response.
No game input is predicted or interpolated.

The target consumer `0x00332938` calls `scePadRead` at `0x00332A24` and converts
the current reply directly into per-player state. SDK read `0x0038FF40` calls
`0x0038FE90` to choose the latest pad-area half, then copies its data. This
path is a current-state snapshot, not a queue of historical key events. UI
edge events are separate from the race's current pad state.

Rendering latency is independent: the GS queue originally allowed 12 vblanks
of lag (`g_gs_max_lag` in `runtime/gs/gs.cpp`). That may add visible latency
under rendering load, and changing it requires separate renderer validation.
Fixing the stale host snapshot alone does not establish that the reported
half-second input-to-image delay is fully resolved.


## ps2/LOD_CULLING_INVESTIGATION
# LOD, distance and visibility investigation


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/LOD_CULLING_INVESTIGATION.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `2f8c470f7c44eb07ad2ef858f5dde9217d72f19202c2b770d66f5c4f85961134`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


Static investigation, 2026-10-16. No gameplay changes, builds, game runs or GPU
measurements were made for this document. Addresses refer to the supported
`SLUS_209.10` (3,368,996 bytes, ordinary CRC32 `75BB93EE`). Evidence is local
retail ELF disassembly, generated recompilation and the cited read
in place. This is a bounded first-hook investigation, not a completed streaming
or visibility audit.

## Outcome and scope

A concrete first implementation target exists: an opt-in **car LOD threshold
multiplier after native car loading at `0021ABF8`**, preceded by a read-only
trace of the loaded threshold/model arrays. The engine already loads each car's
available model levels during initialization; its visual selectors compare
camera distance with an array of thresholds. This is more precise than
increasing an option value or disabling visibility tests. Preserve the original
mode as the default and leave simulation, physics, AI and timing untouched.

Treat car LOD retention, track submission range, projection/fog distance and
frustum edge correctness as separate settings/investigations. This pass supports
improving car model retention; it does **not** establish unlimited track distance
or zero pop-in. Highest available detail means an existing valid game asset,
not extra polygons or texels synthesized by rendering at 4K/8K.

The quality ceiling must accommodate much faster future Macs and PCs, including
RTX 5090 class hardware at 8K, rather than stop at the cited. Keep an
efficient playable Mac preset and allow explicitly expensive Maximum/Extreme
presets. Profile EE CPU selection/submission, guest memory/residency, texture
loading and GPU raster cost separately. Extra GPU throughput and upscaling
cannot remove CPU submission or absent/residency limitations.  no DLSS investigation
or Windows implementation is part of this work.

## The original draw-distance option is not an unbounded multiplier

Disassemble with `.venv/bin/python tools/dis.py -f 00212808`.

`00212808` defaults the option to 2, reads `draw_distance`, initializes a float
factor to zero, and branches only for options 0, 1 and 2:

| Raw option | Intermediate factor | Final float at `00495D58` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0.5 | 1150 |
| 1 | 0.25 | 725 |
| 2 (default) | 0 | 300 |
| Other integer | 0 | 300 |

The final expression is `1700 * factor + 300` (`002128C8`–`00212900`). These
are engine world-distance values; this pass does not assert metres. Raising the
integer past 2 cannot extend the range. This corrects the historical suggestion
in MODDING_SCOPE §1.3. The option ordering also must not be inferred from its
integer magnitude.

The setup calls native projection `0034E530` with near=1, far=`00495D58` and
FOV approximately 0.654498 radians (`00212930`–`00212948`). Initialization at
`002127B0` separately uses near=1, far=1000, FOV=67.5 degrees. Actual race calls
can replace these values; the camera trace documented in NATIVE_CAMERA_ASPECT
already observes other FOVs.

`00212B58` reads the same distance, divides it by the result of `00211378`
clamped to [1,4], and passes the quotient to projection at `00212C04`.
`00211378` reads `003D1A74`, a view/player-count-related global also used by
car LOD scaling. The fog-related call `0033ECB8` receives distance-dependent
arguments at `00212C34`. Thus a far-plane-only experiment can leave fog or other
range consumers inconsistent. Two views can use a reduced native distance;
verify actual values per view rather than assuming one-player settings carry
unchanged into split screen.

`00212DB0` and `00212DC0` are identical getters for `00495D58`. The simple
`tools/dis.py -x` JAL search finds no callers; this is **not** proof that there
are no tail-call/indirect/data references. A write after setup is a candidate
range experiment only after logging later projection/fog updates and other
scene limits. Do not patch a getter and assume the whole engine changed.

## Asset availability and the distinction between disk and live residency

A fresh in-place directory scan of all 37 `DATA/*/*.CAR` archives found:

- 31 contain `Low0.mod` through `Low4.mod`.
- Five contain `Low0.mod` through `Low3.mod`.
- One contains `Low0.mod` through `Low6.mod`.
- Every one of these Low model entries lies before the archive's extractable
  boundary (`dir_offset + header[0x1C]`), in its resident prefix.
- No `lod_hi.val` entry occurs in the scanned CAR/TRK/RES archives.
- All 15 GRAF track scene entries also lie in resident prefixes. Their sizes
  range from the 1,788-byte empty track to 3,993,276 bytes for Homebase;
  Afton's GRAF is 3,435,712 bytes.
- The archive scan finds 1,547 `.tm0` texture variants. Unlike the Low models,
  these belong to the known extractable/on-demand texture path.

These facts establish on-disc availability and archive grouping, **not** that
all tracks/cars stay live simultaneously. Resource sets, model instances and
texture budgets can still be released or bounded at runtime. The recomp retains
the original guest memory model; faster host hardware alone does not expand
its allocators. No evidence here supports streaming an arbitrarily large world.

For a concrete example, `ALGAR.CAR` contains Low0/1/2/3/4 sizes of
14,516 / 161,380 / 155,348 / 36,084 / 10,820 bytes. Do not force index zero on
the assumption it is the highest-detail playable car. Its `lod.val` says:

```
low:     lod0="0 n", lod1="10 y", lod2="15 y", lod3="30 y", lod4="500 y"
detail5: min=1, mirror=3, scale=1.0, use=low
shadow:  lod0=0, lod1=10, lod2=70, model=shadow
```

Whitespace in the retail values contains tabs. Other vehicles have exceptions
(e.g. bus 12/17/30/500, some 40 instead of 30, trailers with fewer levels or
1010). All 37 have a `detail5` table with min=1 and scale=1.0; mirror/shadow
fields differ. Use the loaded table per vehicle, never one hard-coded global
array or a presumed five-level count. Packet byte sizes are not polygon counts
and do not establish which visual elements each model contains.

The loader `0021ABF8` checks `high_detail_car` through `00212DF0`, probes
`%s.car/lod_hi.val`, and falls back to `%s.car/lod.val` when the high table
is absent (`0021AC40`–`0021AC98`). This option cannot conjure absent models.
The loader selects an available `detailN` table from `detail_level`, resolves
its `use` table, reads min/mirror, and parses each `lodN` with `%f %s`
(`0021B014`–`0021B098`). The `y` flag becomes a separate record field; changing
it is outside the proposed LOD-distance experiment.

The loader iterates all parsed levels and calls model loader `0034CEF0` for
`%s%d.mod` at `0021B640`–`0021B6F0`, storing per-level model handles. This is
positive static evidence for initializing the complete selected model chain,
rather than loading only the currently visible mesh on every transition.
Live handle/allocator traces are still needed. Texture helper `003545B8`
constructs a `.tm0` name, loads it via `001323E8`, checks TEX version 10 and
feeds `003537F0`; texture promotion/eviction timing has not been traced.

## Actual LOD selection and submission

The visual car object passed as a0 to `0021ABF8` has these observed fields:

| Offset | Evidence-backed role |
| --- | --- |
| +0x1F8 | Parsed LOD count |
| +0x220 | Pointer to records, stride 16 bytes |
| record+0 | Float threshold |
| record+4 | Parsed `y` flag |
| record+8 / +12 | Model-part capability flags from loaded models |
| +0x74 | Per-level model handle array (indexed with stride 4) |
| +0x548 | Camera distance multiplied by view/FOV factors |
| +0x54C | Selected LOD index |
| +0x550 | Minimum permitted index from selected detail table |

`0021C6E0` performs a single-object selection. `00218E68` begins with an
equivalent loop over the car pointers at `003D1C90`, up to 20 objects. Both:

1. Compute Euclidean camera distance with `0034FA98` from object+0x28.
2. Multiply by the FOV compensation returned by `0034F620` and the count-related
   factor from `00211318`. The four retail factors at `004062A8` are 1,1,2,2.
3. Start with the last available index, choose the first record whose threshold
   is strictly greater than scaled distance, then clamp to the minimum and count.
4. Store the result at object+0x54C.

For Algar this retains index1 until scaled distance reaches10, then index2
until15, index3 until30 and index4 afterward. This is a model-quality switch,
separate from the 300/725/1150 projection range. Wider FOV also affects the
LOD distance compensation; merely extending the far plane does not retain
higher model detail.

Submission consumes the selection: `002189C8` indexes a per-level handle array
at +0x21C with +0x54C and submits through `0034BDA8` at `00218AEC`/`00218B10`.
The companion model arrays are initialized by the loader. `00218C38` also reads
selected-record flags for wheel/part rendering. Hence model identity, wheels,
damage and mirrors must be checked together; forcing a numeric index without
respecting these arrays would be unsafe.

## Frustum coupling and wide edges

Native `0034E530` changes the half-FOV tangent using xScale at `003DD658`,
then stores near/far at `004CD370`/`004CD374`, tan/cot half-FOV coefficients at
`004CD378`/`004CD37C` and additional sphere-test coefficients at
`004CD380`/`004CD384`. It also updates native packet projection through
`0035E120`. The matrix compensation already documented in
NATIVE_CAMERA_ASPECT remains relevant; GS output aspect alone is insufficient.

`0034E308` is a concrete **CPU sphere-versus-view test**, taking centre a0
and radius f12, with optional classification/distance outputs a1/a2. It subtracts
camera position `004CD31C`, dots with the camera basis, rejects before near or
after far including radius, then tests absolute side-axis components against a
bound derived from depth*`004CD378` plus radius*`004CD380`. It uses the same
broad bound for both side axes and additional conservative inside-classification
constants. Do not rewrite it as an assumed canonical six-plane test without
establishing the engine coordinate conventions.

There is direct scene-submission evidence: the call at `0034C0EC` is followed
by a zero-result branch at `0034C0F4` that skips the subsequent submission work.
`0034CCD4` likewise calls this test and gates `0034B140`; wrappers `0034F630`
and `0034F650` expose the test to other callers. Thus this is an appropriate
read-only visibility diagnostic hook. The CPU test consumes the same widened
FOV coefficient generated by native camera setup; there is no evidence that
it is simply stuck at a fixed 4:3 constant. It remains necessary to inspect
track traversal, additional rejection layers and VU clipping for edge loss.

**No culling bypass is justified.** Current 16:10 scene evidence supports
proportions/Hor+ but is not an ultrawide edge-visibility test. Per-view projection
state and temporary targets must be logged separately. Extending output aspect
requires the native scale relation `(4/3)/outputAspect`, correct presentation,
and these actual CPU/VU/scene tests to agree. Current support for named host
aspect modes does not itself implement arbitrary ultrawide output.

## Next implementation target and acceptance

First add bounded, opt-in read-only wrappers (preserve all native side effects):
`0021ABF8` records per-car thresholds/min/count and loaded handles after return;
`0021C6E0` records distance/index; `0034E308` samples input/output and current
near/far/FOV/camera state. Batch selector `00218E68` also needs before/after
sampling because it selects and submits within one call; a post-return LOD
forcing wrapper there would be too late. Reuse the existing projection trace.
No production behavior hook was added in this pass.

The first behavioral experiment should multiply **only positive car thresholds**
at the end of `0021ABF8` by a finite, validated setting >=1 (1 preserves the
baseline). Retain zero, all flags, model handles, count, min, shadow tables and
original physics data. This single load-time hook feeds both selectors and
avoids duplicated per-frame patches. A large multiplier keeps the highest
permitted model longer; do not use infinity or overwrite all thresholds with
one value. This is a supported candidate, not a verified safe implementation:
confirm array ownership/lifetime, float bounds and all handle entries in trace
before enabling it. A finite distance profile can subsequently set the first
permitted threshold beyond the intended draw range while preserving ordering.

Validate faithful/multiplier1 identity, distant opponents moving both ways across
thresholds, damage/detached panels/wheels, mirrors, trailers, one/two views and
4:3/16:10/16:9/ultrawide edge sweeps. Sample selected indexes and handles alongside
images, EE frame time, submission/primitive counts, texture I/O and guest/host
memory. Raise scene/projection/fog distance in a **separate** experiment after
tracing its other limits. Check wider scene bounds before judging absence as
frustum failure. Maximum presets may exceed full-speed performance on the M2
Pro; report that honestly without lowering simulation load or quality silently.

The investigation stops here because a concrete asset-backed load-time hook
and actual CPU visibility consumer are established. Outstanding work is live
residency/allocator verification, track traversal/range limits, texture
promotion, complete per-view/VU edge testing and measured performance. Literal
zero pop-in remains unproven.


## ps2/LOD_RUNTIME
# Car LOD runtime experiment


:::note Source and evidence
PS2 implementation notes. Preserve each claim’s original evidence limits. Static disassembly, CPU tests, proposals and live gameplay validation are different evidence levels. See [Battle recovery](/ps2/BATTLE_RECOVERY) for the current native weapon contract.

Source: `docs/LOD_RUNTIME.md` in `eod-recomp`. Repository HEAD: `67c972b0fed775994d1769382676bd94ebdc3bc7`. Working-copy modifications: `no`. Source SHA-256: `e9abdf8bf6335b07fa2f774afc76ba8aef11b7e77c67fb5c01fdb610570c1863`. Imported 2026-10-19. Addresses belong only to the platform/revision identified in the source; do not transfer Xbox addresses to PS2.
:::


2026-10-16. Full Mac build and runtime traces now verify the first bounded
experiment. Two headless/muted 5000-vblank two-player runs completed with exit0;
all20 loaded car tables validated in baseline and multiplier2. The tables logged
expected native/effective thresholds and model handles. Camera/motion diverged
between the captures, so they are not accepted as a matched visual LOD comparison.
Broader visual/performance acceptance remains open. Track traversal,
fog, far-plane extension and ultrawide edge correctness remain separate work.

## Controls and bounded output

`EOD_LOD_TRACE=1` enables diagnostics on the EE thread. Like `EOD_CAMERA_TRACE`,
presence enables it (unset it to disable). Combine both for actual projection
inputs and later CPU visibility consumers. Defaults preserve native behavior.

* `0021ABF8`: after native loading, up to 64 tables and their individual levels:
  owner object, record/count/handle addresses, min, count, original/effective
  thresholds, all three record flags, original and active handles.
* `0021C6E0`: first 16 calls, then every 120th, maximum 128 lines: selected
  index/handle, scaled distance, minimum, current near/far and view-count global.
* `00218E68`: before/after the entire native selection/submission call; first two
  calls, then every 120th, at most 64 groups of up to 20 cars. After-call output
  observes the result; it does not alter submission already performed inside.
* `0034E308`: actual CPU sphere visibility result, first 16 calls then every
  4096th, maximum 128 lines. Captures caller RA, centre/radius, camera position,
  near/far and native tangent/sphere coefficients. Optional output pointers are
  shown as raw post-call words because native early rejects can leave them
  unwritten. This diagnostic does not infer a canonical six-plane frustum.

Invalid-load/rejected-multiplier diagnostics share a 64-line error budget. A
fresh process resets budgets and reads the multiplier again. Sparse samples
avoid turning a long race into unbounded logging; they do not capture every
transition or establish a per-frame performance measurement.

`EOD_CAR_LOD_MULTIPLIER=2` requests a load-time experiment. The parser accepts
only finite float values >=1; malformed/NaN/infinite/overflow values log once
and use 1. A table is changed only after its full validation: own embedded
records/count, count 1..16, valid minimum, original handles other than the native
`-1` sentinel, finite nondecreasing thresholds and finite scaled results. The
entire table is rejected before any write if validation fails. Multiply only
strictly positive thresholds; preserve signed zero and negative values. At 1,
no guest writes occur. Flags, min/count, model handles, shadow tables, physics,
simulation and the native selector are untouched. Do not infer that numeric
handle zero is invalid: these are opaque native handles, not guest pointers.

No preset or local build enables the experiment. High factors may
exceed playable rendering/submission cost and have not been accepted visually.

## Concrete layout corrections and ABI evidence

Generated `gen/rec_046.c` function `00217DF0` stores these pointers before calling
the loader; confirmed with the retail ELF disassembler, not only the earlier
investigation's prose:

| Field | Role |
| --- | --- |
| object+0x74 | Original loaded model handles, four-byte stride |
| object+0xB4 | Active handle copies, initially duplicated by loader |
| object+0xF8 | Embedded 16-byte LOD records, capacity 16 |
| object+0x1F8 | Embedded native count |
| object+0x21C | Pointer to active handles, initially object+0xB4 |
| object+0x220 | Pointer to records, initially object+0xF8 |
| object+0x224 | **Pointer to count**, initially object+0x1F8 |
| object+0x548 / +0x54C / +0x550 | Scaled distance / selected index / minimum |

The earlier investigation omitted +0x224 and did not distinguish active from
original handles. `0021C130` explicitly aliases a different object's +0x74,
+0xF8 and +0x1F8 into a clone's three pointers. Thus editing every object each
frame could compound shared thresholds. This implementation only writes the
owning loader's freshly parsed embedded records; both selectors and clones
consume that storage naturally. A loader call reparses every threshold before
scaling, so reloading an owner does not multiply the prior edited thresholds.

Loader `0021ABF8` preserves entry a0 in s4 (`R[20]`); its loop at `0021B640`
calls `0034CEF0`, stores the return handle into +0x74 and +0xB4, then writes
capability flags at record+8/+12. Both selectors load the count **through**
+0x224 and compare scaled distance strictly `< threshold`, then clamp to min
and count. Disassembly checked `0021C130` and `0021C6E0`; generated bodies also
checked `00217DF0`, `0021ABF8`, `00218E68` and `0034E308`.

`tools/recomp.py` generates every guest function as `void f_ADDRESS(void)` using
global `g_ee`; `wrap` renames only the native definition to `_orig` and retains
calls/table entries pointing at the runtime wrapper. Each wrapper snapshots
needed input in host locals, calls `_orig` exactly once, then performs plain
memory/log operations. It does not restore entry registers over native results
or call any guest helper. CPU tests check all bytes of EEState, including upper
GPR halves, FPR/FACC/FCC/SP/RA, and native memory side effects after each wrapper.
This is the local synchronous generator ABI; it does not use Road Trip's
scheduler-resume wrapping API.

## Reuse research

Rechecked online RoadTripAdventure-recomp main at commit
`0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8` on 2026-10-16:
[src/game/overrides.cpp](https://github.com/silentsudin/RoadTripAdventure-recomp/blob/0f6d3613e8e32ccda5305227a578b1fb659983a8/src/game/overrides.cpp).
Its `buildCameraWide`/`setFrustumScale` narrow projection matrices for the two
player cameras and separately widen the game's seven EE ground-tile frustum
points. `finishIfDone`/resume hooks apply postprocessing only when the camera
builder really returns after scheduler checkpoints. Reusable approach: scope
visual changes to verified native consumers, retain unmodified originals, and
keep CPU traversal bounds consistent with projection. Its hardcoded camera/
frustum addresses and `R5900Context`/`PS2Runtime` registration cannot be transplanted
into EOD's different ELF, visibility equations and global-state generator.
The inspected source contains no generic car LOD threshold hook to reuse.

## Integration and CPU verification

Add `src/hle_lod.cpp` to the runtime HLE sources in CMake. Add a CPU-only target
with `tools/tests/lod_runtime_test.cpp` and `src/hle_lod.cpp`; include directories
`runtime`, `runtime/include`, `src`. Invoke it separately with `off`, `one`,
`two`, `trace`, and `invalid` (environment is cached per process). No game asset
or graphics library is needed for this target. HLE config adds four `wrap`
entries. Regenerate the normal ignored game sources once integration is ready:

```
.venv/bin/python tools/recomp.py
```

Focused verification performed with Clang C++17 `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, linking
the production wrapper. All five modes passed. Tests cover multiplier parsing,
identity including negative zero, overflow/unordered/count rejection, full guest
memory equality when off/1/trace/invalid, exact positive-word-only mutation at 2,
clone aliases, invalid handles, transactional rejection, and register/native
side-effect preservation. Stub native calls are explicitly not real-game proof.
No full CMake configure/regeneration/build, game launch or GPU run was performed
for this source checkpoint.

## Initial game evidence and remaining acceptance

contracts); logs `work/hud-build.log` and `work/hud-ctest.log`. The gameplay
experiment remains opt-in, without changing the local build.

## Remaining game acceptance

Coordinate with any renderer measurement and use headless/muted automation:
`EOD_HEADLESS=1 EOD_MUTE=1`, executable `--headless`. First run with
`EOD_LOD_TRACE=1 EOD_CAMERA_TRACE=1` and multiplier unset. Capture tables for real
cars/trailers; confirm finite ordered thresholds, valid min/count, handles and
record ownership/aliasing. Confirm single/batch outputs choose native levels and
capture current far/tangent values in race visibility samples. Compare unset
against multiplier1 for baseline images/state, then trial2 in a separate run.

Acceptance needs opponents moving both ways across thresholds, wheels/damage/
detached panels, mirrors, trailers, one/two views, and 4:3/16:10/16:9/ultrawide
edge sweeps. Compare selected indexes **and handles** with images, EE/submission
cost and memory/texture activity. CPU tests cannot certify assets remain resident,
no pop-in, edge coverage or full-speed rendering. Extend projection/fog/track
range only in a separate traced experiment; do not disable native culling or
